effect_estimate.comment: Quantitative observational comparisons (Kruskal-Wallis tests) and unbalanced static fixed-effects panel regressions without confidence intervals reported; exact index means, 5-year differences, regression slopes, and p-values extracted from Tables 7, 9, 11, 13, and 14.
effect_estimate.value: In 2010 cross-sectional Kruskal-Wallis comparisons across SNIS providers (N = 1,203 total; valid index N = 86 to 1,196), private companies ranked 1st or 2nd among major provider types on 9 of 14 indicators: higher sewage collection (IN015 mean = 70.05% vs. 69.70% direct public administration, 67.51% regional authority, and 41.79% mixed-capital public management; N = 525, p = 0.000), higher sewage treatment (IN016 = 80.23% vs. 42.94% direct public, 55.14% regional, 68.60% mixed-capital public; N = 611, p = 0.000), higher treated sewage relative to water consumed (IN046 = 55.28% vs. 32.83% direct public, 31.60% regional, 25.59% mixed-capital public; N = 524, p = 0.006), 2nd in total water service coverage (IN055 = 79.18% vs. 82.86% regional, 77.42% mixed-capital public, 76.71% direct public; N = 985, p = 0.032) and water fluoridation (IN057 = 62.76% vs. 73.34% regional, 57.04% mixed-capital public, 45.29% direct public; N = 836, p = 0.000), while charging intermediate average tariffs (IN004 = 1.89 vs. 0.84 direct public, 1.26 regional, 2.21 mixed-capital public; N = 862, p = 0.000). From 2006 to 2010, private companies had the 2nd highest per-capita investment (mean R$ 32.22 vs. R$ 39.57 mixed-capital private management, R$ 26.70 mixed-capital public, R$ 22.24 direct public, R$ 17.10 regional; p = 0.0001). From 2005 to 2010 (excluding providers that changed legal nature), private companies achieved the largest coverage gains in sewage collection (ΔIN015 = +26.28 percentage points vs. +3.10 direct public and +2.19 regional; p = 0.013) and sewage treatment (ΔIN046 = +39.36 vs. +5.75 direct public and +9.13 regional; p = 0.000), with no significant difference in water service growth (ΔIN055 = -0.73 vs. -3.58 direct public and -0.90 regional; p = 0.634). In static municipality fixed-effects panel regressions (2000, 2005, 2010), private companies showed the strongest or tied-strongest tariff responsiveness (IN004) to cost/productivity indexes in 8 of 10 specifications (e.g., operational expenditure per m3 billed IN026 slope β1 = 1.1457, p = 0.000 vs. public differential γ2 = -0.2046, p = 0.049 and mixed-capital differential γ3 = -0.2613, p = 0.018).
